# 7.1 Document Deletion Execution Methods

> "deleteOne(filter) deletes the first document that matches a query filter. deleteMany(filter) deletes every document that matches a query filter. Passing an empty filter ({}) deletes all documents in the collection, without dropping the collection itself."

## 1. Operational Overview & Execution Context

MongoDB provides two CRUD Delete methods scoped by match cardinality: `db.<collection>.deleteOne(<filter>)` removes the first document satisfying `<filter>`, while `db.<collection>.deleteMany(<filter>)` removes all matching documents (including total collection truncation when passed an empty filter `{}`).

The diagram above illustrates the three core deletion patterns: targeted single-record removal via `deleteOne({ name: "Kabir" })`, filtered bulk removal via `deleteMany({ age: 17 })`, and collection truncation via `deleteMany({})`.

Within the broader parent module (**7. Document Deletion & Collection Pruning (CRUD Delete)**), sub-topic `7.1` governs day-to-day developer workflows, driver execution behavior, and return telemetry.

## 2. Detailed Sub-Mechanism & Parameter Analysis

### 2.1 Single-Target Deletion (`deleteOne(filter)`)

`deleteOne(<filter>)` deletes at most `1` document—specifically the first document matching `<filter>`—and returns `{ acknowledged: true, deletedCount: 1 }` (or `deletedCount: 0` if no document matched).

### 2.2 Multi-Target Deletion (`deleteMany(filter)`) & Truncation (`deleteMany({})`)

`deleteMany(<filter>)` deletes all documents matching `<filter>` and returns `{ acknowledged: true, deletedCount: N }`. Passing an empty filter `{}` (`db.students.deleteMany({})`) deletes all documents in the collection without dropping the collection container or its indexes.

## 3. Production `mongosh` Workflows & Return Telemetry

The following `mongosh` implementation demonstrates practical operational patterns, parameter combinations, and server acknowledgment telemetry for this sub-topic.

```javascript
// 1. Single-document deletion (removes first match only)
db.students.deleteOne({ name: "Kabir" });
// Output: { acknowledged: true, deletedCount: 1 }

// 2. Filtered multi-document deletion
db.students.deleteMany({ age: 17 });
db.students.deleteMany({ grade: 7 });

// 3. Empty filter ({}) deletes all documents without dropping the collection
db.students.deleteMany({});
```

Always inspect the acknowledgment object or return payload emitted by `mongosh` to confirm that your operation matched and affected the expected namespace or document set.

## 4. Operational Execution Pipeline Diagram

The architectural flowchart below traces the decision branches, parameter validations, and execution outcomes across the L-2 and L-3 mindmap nodes.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["CRUD Delete Call"] --> B{"Method & Filter?"}
    B -->|deleteOne(filter)| C["Deletes First Matching Document Only"]
    B -->|deleteMany(filter)| D["Deletes Every Document Matching Filter"]
    B -->|deleteMany({})| E["Deletes All Documents; Preserves Collection & Indexes"]
```

Understanding these operational branches prevents common runtime bugs during application development and database administration.

## 5. Multi-Dimension Comparison Matrix & Developer Pitfalls

| Method Call | Filter Type | Documents Deleted | Return Object |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `deleteOne({ name: "Kabir" })` | Equality filter | First match only (`0` or `1`) | `{ acknowledged: true, deletedCount: 0\|1 }` |
| `deleteMany({ age: 17 })` | Equality filter | All matching documents (`0..N`) | `{ acknowledged: true, deletedCount: N }` |
| `deleteMany({})` | Empty filter `{}` | 100% of documents in collection | `{ acknowledged: true, deletedCount: Total }` |

### Key Exam Traps & Takeaways

- **High-Frequency Exam Trap — `deleteMany()` vs. `deleteMany({})`**: Calling `find()` with no arguments works, but calling `deleteOne()` or `deleteMany()` with **no arguments** throws an error! You must pass `{}` (`deleteMany({})`).
- **What Does `deleteOne({})` Do?**: Passing an empty filter `{}` to `deleteOne({})` deletes the very first document in the collection.
- **Collection Survival**: Even when `deleteMany({})` deletes every single document (`0` documents left), `show collections` will still list the collection!
